question: Explain the preconditions for an audit that the auditor must establish before accepting an engagement under SA 210.
sources: SA 210 Agreeing the Terms of Audit Engagements

points.label: Meaning of preconditions
points.description: Preconditions are the use by management of an acceptable financial reporting framework and management's agreement to the premise on which the audit is conducted.
points.basis: SA 210, definition of preconditions for an audit

points.label: Acceptable framework
points.description: The auditor checks whether the financial reporting framework to be used in preparing the financial statements is acceptable.
points.basis: SA 210, determining acceptability of the financial reporting framework

points.label: Responsibility for financial statements
points.description: Management acknowledges its responsibility for preparing the financial statements as per the framework, including fair presentation where relevant.

points.label: Responsibility for internal control
points.description: Management acknowledges its responsibility for the internal control needed to prepare financial statements free from material misstatement, whether due to fraud or error.

points.label: Access to information and persons
points.description: Management agrees to give the auditor access to all relevant information, any additional information requested, and unrestricted access to people in the entity; if the preconditions are not present the auditor should not accept the engagement unless required by law.
points.basis: SA 210, agreement of management responsibilities; limitation on acceptance
